lines.text: One more problem, and it's sneaky. What if a camera is mounted just one degree crooked?
Then every tag it sees looks shifted sideways, about one point seven centimeters for every meter of distance.
Every photo is wrong the same way, so averaging a thousand of them still gives the same wrong answer.
It's like a bathroom scale that always reads one kilogram heavy. Weighing ten times won't fix it. Zeroing it once will.
So we calibrate each camera once. The robot is pushed onto a real scoring spot with a jig, so its position is known exactly.
Then it backs straight away, slowly, for zero point six meters. It knows where the tag should appear in every photo.
Each camera compares what it saw with what it should have seen, and learns its own small fix, good for every tag.
And we use two cameras on the front corners. They see the tag from the sides, where its tilt is clear.
